what_happened: Every carried figure in the seed report's blanket 'MEASURED 2026-11-10' framing turned out to have a different, individually-stale origin: suite count is 149(claimed)/157(core source-store)/189(this repo's deployed tree)/197(all-extensions source-store)/204(verify-deploy.sh's own live corpus scan), depending on counting scope; gate8=662,462ms in gate-cost-model.csv is dated 2026-10-19 inside the file itself; test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh's 543000ms hint-file row has been unchanged since 2026-10-16 (git -S search), a month before the claimed measurement date. None of these were re-measured by any commit since.

Applying the owner's DELETE/KEEP discrimination rule suite-by-suite (not just by lexical grep match) revealed that the lexical 'mentions run-all.sh|verify-deploy.sh' grep used by the seed report over-counts by ~2.6x: of 36 grep hits only 14 are genuine 'recursive meta-suite' class members (the owner's actual target), 9 are narrow unit/lint suites that merely use verify-deploy.sh as test subject or plumbing, and 13 are comment-only or planted-fixture-content false positives (e.g. test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh and test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh never execute the real scripts they mention). Within the true 14-member class, every one tests a cross-invocation, concurrency, or crash-safety property that a single real-tree gate run structurally cannot self-certify, so the correct verdict for all 14 is KEEP, not DELETE -- this prevents the plan/implement phases from wrongly deleting suites that look redundant under a naive grep but are not redundant under the owner's own stated rule.

Re-confirmed live: 1716 /tmp/tmp.* entries, 1.4GB, oldest dated 2026-11-10 (the date of the one prior manual sweep), growing continuously since. Confirmed at least 5 of a 400-entry sample still carry chmod-a-w'd (read-only) nested content requiring chmod -R u+w before rm -rf would succeed, reproducing leak mechanism 2 from the seed report exactly. No /tmp/tmp.* reaper exists anywhere in claude-refresh.sh or skill-refresh.

Direct live timing isolated the cost lever exactly: script-inventory.sh --size-line costs 2.37s on the repo root and 2.22s on a non-git rsync fixture, out of 4.07s total for verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 1 -- so the corpus probe is ~58% of a minimal gate-narrowed invocation and fires in BOTH fixture shapes the expensive suites use. Refines the research report's blanket '~4.6s fixed corpus-scan overhead' attribution (the whole invocation is 4.07s today) and makes the savings estimate arithmetic rather than conjectural.

The research report's Context Extension Recommendation targets agent-system/extensions/core/context/standards/shell-script-testing.md, which is in concurrent sibling task 604's declared file_scope this same cycle, and whose index-entries.json line_count entry (1373) would additionally need regeneration. The plan redirects that documentation to a specs/decisions/ verdict record plus a pointer comment in tests/run-all.sh's own header, keeping this task's file_scope disjoint from both siblings and from any coupled generated surface.
